questions.title: How does backpropagation work through a 4-bit NF4 quantized weight matrix?
questions.question_body: In the QLoRA paper, gradients are backpropagated through a frozen, 4-bit quantized pretrained model into LoRA adapters. I understand that during the forward pass the NF4 weights are dequantized to BFloat16 before matrix multiplication, but I’m unclear how the backward pass computes the gradient w.r.t. the dequantized weights. Specifically, do we need to compute \(\frac{\partial E}{\partial \mathbf{W}}\) for the quantized matrix, or is it enough to compute \(\frac{\partial E}{\partial \mathbf{L}_i}\) for the LoRA parameters? How are the quantization constants involved in the gradient chain rule, and does the quantization introduce any bias in the gradient estimates?

questions.title: What is the exact definition of the NF4 data type and how does it differ from standard 4‑bit Float or Int representations?
questions.question_body: The paper introduces a 4‑bit NormalFloat (NF4) that is said to be information‑theoretically optimal for zero‑centered normal distributions. The construction mentions using quantiles of a standard normal and creating an asymmetric set to include a zero point. Can someone lay out the precise codebook values for NF4, explain why a zero point must be added, and show a concrete example of quantizing and dequantizing a small tensor (e.g., a 2×2 matrix) with NF4 compared to Int4?

questions.title: Why does Double Quantization reduce memory by ~0.37 bits per parameter and how are the two levels of constants stored?
questions.question_body: Double Quantization (DQ) treats the first‑level scaling factors \(c_2^{\text{FP32}}\) as inputs to a second quantizer producing 8‑bit floats \(c_2^{\text{FP8}}\) and associated higher‑level constants \(c_1^{\text{FP32}}\). The paper claims that for a blocksize of 64 this reduces the overhead from 0.5 bits/param to 0.127 bits/param. I’m having trouble reproducing this calculation. Could anyone walk through the arithmetic step‑by‑step, clarify why we subtract the mean before quantizing \(c_2\), and describe how these two levels of constants are accessed during dequantization?

questions.title: How do Paged Optimizers avoid gradient checkpointing spikes without slowing down training?
questions.question_body: The authors say that NVIDIA Unified Memory is used to page optimizer states between GPU and CPU when memory spikes occur during gradient checkpointing. How exactly is this integrated into the optimizer loop? Does paging happen automatically per tensor, or do we need to manually allocate "paged" buffers? Also, under what circumstances might paging cause a noticeable slowdown, and are there any best‑practice hyperparameters (e.g., sequence length, batch size) to keep paging overhead minimal?

questions.title: Why do default LoRA hyperparameters (e.g., adapters only on Q/K projections) fail to match full‑model finetuning performance on large models?
questions.question_body: Figure 1 in the paper shows that adding LoRA adapters to *all* linear layers, not just query/value projections, is crucial for matching full finetuning on LLaMA‑7B. Is there an intuitive explanation for why limiting adapters harms performance? Does this relate to which parts of the transformer contribute most to instruction following, or is it simply a matter of capacity (more trainable parameters)?

questions.title: What is the rationale behind using BFloat16 as the computation datatype while storing weights in NF4?
questions.question_body: QLoRA stores model weights in 4‑bit NF4 but performs forward/backward matrix multiplications in BFloat16. Why not use Float16 or FP8 for computation? Are there specific numerical stability or hardware support reasons for preferring BFloat16 in this setting?

questions.title: How does the Elo rating aggregation work for chatbot evaluation in QLoRA?
questions.question_body: The paper describes building a tournament from pairwise comparisons (human or GPT‑4) and then computing Elo scores with K=32 over 10 000 random seeds. I’m unsure how ties are handled in Elo updates, how seeds affect ordering, and whether match outcomes are weighted by confidence scores from annotators. Could someone provide a concise algorithmic description of this Elo computation as used in the paper?

questions.title: Why does strong MMLU performance not correlate with Vicuna chatbot benchmark scores?
questions.question_body: The authors observe that models fine‑tuned on FLAN‑v2 excel on MMLU but perform poorly on Vicuna, while OASST1 fine‑tuned models show the opposite trend. Is this purely due to dataset similarity, or could it be because MMLU favors factual recall while Vicuna rewards conversational style? How could one design an evaluation suite that jointly captures both abilities?

questions.title: Can QLoRA be extended beyond 4‑bit (e.g., 3‑bit) quantization without performance loss?
questions.question_body: The paper mentions that more aggressive quantization (e.g., 3‑bit GPTQ) might still recover performance after LoRA finetuning, but this was not explored. What are the main technical obstacles when moving from NF4 to a hypothetical NF3? Would double quantization still save memory, and would gradient flow through an even coarser codebook be stable?

questions.title: How does the “zero point” handling differ between NF4 and traditional symmetric quantizers?
questions.question_body: In Section 3.1, NF4 is built as an asymmetric datatype so that exactly one code value maps to zero – unlike symmetric quantizers where zero may not be representable if an odd number of levels is used. How does this affect dequantization error for sparse tensors (e.g., padded positions), and does it influence training stability compared to using Int4 with an explicit zero code?
